title: Hot Dog Bun (wheat or cracked wheat)

content.title: About
content.content: A hot dog bun is a soft, slightly sweet roll made from wheat or whole‑grain flour, often with added cracked wheat for texture. It is designed to hold sausages, frankfurters and various toppings, and can also serve as a base for small sandwiches.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Traditional hot dog buns are made from white wheat flour, but whole‑grain and cracked‑wheat versions have become popular for added nutrition.
In the United States more than 50 million hot dog buns are consumed each day.
Buns are frequently brushed with a light egg wash and sprinkled with sesame or poppy seeds for flavor and appearance.
In Japan similar rolls are called “hot‑dog” and are often served with mayo and soy sauce.
The dough is proofed in a warm environment to create a light, airy crumb.

items.title: Source of carbohydrates
items.content: Buns provide a quick source of energy through easily digestible carbs.

items.title: Contains fiber (whole‑grain version)
items.content: Whole‑grain buns are rich in dietary fiber, supporting healthy digestion.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Wheat flour supplies thiamine, niacin and folate, important for metabolism.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: Buns contain iron, magnesium and phosphorus, which contribute to bone and blood health.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Unlike many baked goods, hot dog buns typically contain only a small amount of fat.

items.title: Wheat allergy or gluten intolerance
items.content: People with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity may experience adverse reactions to wheat buns.

items.title: High glycemic index
items.content: Buns can cause a rapid rise in blood sugar, which may be problematic for diabetics.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Some recipes add salt, so those monitoring sodium intake should check the label.

items.title: Preservatives and additives
items.content: Commercial buns may contain flavor enhancers and preservatives that are not suitable for everyone.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Slice the bun lengthwise, place a hot dog inside, and add mustard, ketchup, pickles, onions, cheese or any favorite toppings. Buns also work well for small sandwiches with ham, cheese and vegetables.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep buns in an airtight bag at room temperature for up to 3 days. For longer storage, freeze them in a bag – they stay fresh for up to 2 months. Warm in the oven or toaster before serving.
